description: The 10 m wind of the newest NOAA GFS run as a flow field. The archive is an Icechunk repository, so the whole lattice is measured server-side in one request per component.

options.content:
The **10 m wind of the newest NOAA GFS run**, drawn as a flow field: one arrow per grid point, its direction and length taken from the archive's `wind_u_10m` and `wind_v_10m`.

**The map's own time bar does not walk the forecast.** It is a sixty-second loop that animates the streaks along the field, and pressing play sets them moving; the field itself is already drawn without it. Dragging that bar changes nothing about which hour you are looking at.

**The hour comes from the picker above**, which re-runs the query. A flow field holds one instant — the panel keeps the first moment a query offers and drops the rest along with the time column — so there is no forecast for a clock to walk.

**Under the wind** paints one of the archive's own variables as a raster, on the same run and the same hour — it comes from the same two numbers the arrows do, so the two can never drift apart. There is no wind speed among the choices because **the archive does not publish one**: it ships `u` and `v` components, and the tile server paints one variable at a time. Set it to *Nothing* for the field alone.

**Grid** trades detail for reach at the same price. Both settings are 49 points and both take about ten seconds, because what a request costs is the number of points, not the ground they cover: *Detail* samples every cell of the archive over 1.5°, *Wide* every other cell over 3°.

**A tile server that has just started can miss the first load**, and says so: *the tile server did not answer*. Opening the archive costs about five seconds per worker, and DuckDB abandons any response that takes more than ten — a ceiling it offers no way to raise. Refreshing is enough; by then the server is warm.

The archive is published by dynamical.org as an **Icechunk** repository, which no ordinary Zarr reader opens: chunk objects are named by opaque identifiers and the map from array coordinates to object lives in a manifest. The tile server resolves it — and it is also the only thing here that can read the archive at all, which is why the whole lattice travels to it as one GeoJSON `FeatureCollection` per component. Two requests, not ninety-eight.

targets.rawSql:
-- One arrow per grid point, in SIX requests: three batches of the lattice, twice,
-- once per wind component.
--
-- Not one request per point. The archive can only be read by the tile server, and
-- asking it point by point is ninety-eight round trips, which DuckDB issues one at
-- a time: measured, 27.7 s, with the first attempt dying on Grafana's timeout.
--
-- And not one request for the whole lattice either, which is where this gets
-- interesting. `/zarr/statistics` takes a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, walks
-- `features` in order and writes a `statistics` object into each one, so the whole
-- lattice does fit in a single call — and that call takes about seven seconds warm.
-- The trouble is the ceiling on the other side: **DuckDB's `http_client` abandons a
-- response after ten seconds** and exposes no setting to change it (`http_timeout`
-- belongs to httpfs and this extension ignores it). Against a cold tile server the
-- same call took 10.0 s and came back empty. Three batches leave the margin.
--
-- Each cell carries its own lat/lon in `properties`, and those come back untouched,
-- so the six answers are joined on the coordinates we sent — never on the order of
-- an array, and never by parsing a geometry back.
--
-- OJO with the variables. This datasource quotes them by itself in a panel query,
-- which is why $pasada and $lead go bare -- but that stops the moment a format
-- modifier appears, so '${store:percentencode}' needs its own quotes or the query
-- dies in `Parser Error: syntax error at or near "%"`. And $paso must arrive as a
-- number to be multiplied, which is what :raw is for.
LOAD http_client; LOAD json;
WITH grid AS (
  -- Seven by seven around 2.75 S, 79 W -- the austro. Generated here, with
  -- integers divided at the end, because the flow layer rejects a lattice whose
  -- spacing wobbles by more than 5% and draws nothing while saying nothing.
  -- Never built from the coordinates the server echoes back.
  SELECT (-275 + i * ${paso:raw}) / 100.0 AS latitude,
         (-7900 + j * ${paso:raw}) / 100.0 AS longitude
  FROM (SELECT unnest(range(-3, 4)) AS i) a,
       (SELECT unnest(range(-3, 4)) AS j) b
), lotes AS (
  -- Modulo rather than division, so the three batches come out the same size
  -- (17, 16, 16) instead of two full ones and a remainder.
  SELECT latitude, longitude,
         (row_number() OVER (ORDER BY latitude, longitude) - 1) % 3 AS lote
  FROM grid
), fc AS (
  SELECT lote, json_group_array(json_object(
           'type', 'Feature',
           'properties', json_object('lat', latitude, 'lon', longitude),
           'geometry', json_object(
             'type', 'Polygon',
             'coordinates', json_array(json_array(
               json_array(longitude - 0.05, latitude - 0.05),
               json_array(longitude - 0.05, latitude + 0.05),
               json_array(longitude + 0.05, latitude + 0.05),
               json_array(longitude + 0.05, latitude - 0.05),
               json_array(longitude - 0.05, latitude - 0.05)))))) AS feats
  FROM lotes GROUP BY lote
), q AS (
  -- The run and the hour are pinned, so what the server hands back is a plain
  -- 2-D field and every cell answers with a single band.
  SELECT 'http://titiler/zarr/statistics?url=' || '${store:percentencode}'
      || '&sel=init_time%3D' || $pasada
      || '&sel=lead_time%3D' || $lead
      || '&variable=' AS base
), resp AS (
  SELECT 'u' AS comp, http_post(
    base || 'wind_u_10m',
    MAP {'content-type': 'application/json'},
    ('{"type":"FeatureCollection","features":' || feats::VARCHAR || '}')::JSON) AS r
  FROM fc, q
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'v', http_post(
    base || 'wind_v_10m',
    MAP {'content-type': 'application/json'},
    ('{"type":"FeatureCollection","features":' || feats::VARCHAR || '}')::JSON)
  FROM fc, q
), vivo AS (
  -- Say what went wrong. A request that fails comes back with status -1 and an
  -- EMPTY body, and casting that to JSON reports `Malformed JSON at byte 0`,
  -- which reads like a bug in the query rather than a server that never answered.
  SELECT comp,
         CASE WHEN (r ->> 'status') = '200' THEN (r ->> 'body')::JSON
              ELSE error('the tile server did not answer: '
                         || coalesce(r ->> 'reason', '?')
                         || ' (status ' || coalesce(r ->> 'status', '?') || ')')::JSON
         END AS body
  FROM resp
), vals AS (
  -- `statistics.*.mean` rather than `statistics.b1.mean`: the band is named after
  -- the axes that survived the sel, and naming it here would tie the query to that
  -- spelling.
  SELECT comp,
         json_extract(f, '$.properties.lat')::DOUBLE AS latitude,
         json_extract(f, '$.properties.lon')::DOUBLE AS longitude,
         json_extract(f, '$.properties.statistics.*.mean')[1]::DOUBLE AS val
  FROM vivo, unnest(json_extract(body, '$.features[*]')) AS t(f)
)
-- `u` and `v` are the aliases the flow layer looks for. wind_u_10m is not among
-- them and none of these roles appears in the Field mapping editor, so the alias
-- is the whole contract. And no time column: the layer keeps one instant only.
SELECT latitude, longitude,
       max(val) FILTER (WHERE comp = 'u') AS u,
       max(val) FILTER (WHERE comp = 'v') AS v
FROM vals
GROUP BY latitude, longitude
ORDER BY latitude, longitude

-- El rasterizado de fondo: la MISMA pasada y la MISMA hora que el viento, porque
-- sale de las mismas dos variables ($pasada y $lead). Ni una consulta ni la otra
-- miran el reloj del mapa, que aqui es el bucle sintetico del trazado.
--
-- Esto no devuelve filas de datos: los papeles zarr_* construyen un dataset aparte
-- (`grafana-B-zarr`) que solo lleva la direccion del almacen, la variable y el
-- color. De ahi que baste una fila -- y que cero filas signifique "sin raster",
-- que es lo que hace la opcion `none` del desplegable.
--
-- El rango y la rampa viajan POR FILA y no como opcion del panel: cada variable
-- vive en su propia escala fisica y una sola no puede servir a un porcentaje y a
-- pascales a la vez.
WITH nubes AS (
  -- Blanco que gana cuerpo con la cobertura: por debajo del 10% no se ve nada.
  SELECT '[[[0,26],[255,255,255,0]],[[26,64],[255,255,255,45]],[[64,115],[255,255,255,95]],'
      || '[[115,166],[255,255,255,150]],[[166,217],[255,255,255,200]],[[217,256],[255,255,255,235]]]'
      AS rampa
), lluvia AS (
  SELECT '[[[0,8],[120,190,255,0]],[[8,32],[110,175,245,60]],[[32,80],[80,145,230,110]],'
      || '[[80,150],[50,110,215,165]],[[150,220],[30,75,190,205]],[[220,256],[20,45,160,235]]]'
      AS rampa
)
SELECT $store AS zarr_url,
       $capa  AS zarr_variable,
       -- Los DOS ejes del cubo van aqui, fijos y separados por coma, y ninguno
       -- como papel temporal.
       --
       -- `zarr_time_dim`/`zarr_time_label` son para un eje que camina el reloj del
       -- mapa, y el panel solo los mira si la consulta trae columna de tiempo
       -- (`readCalendar` devuelve el calendario vacio sin ella). Esta no la trae, a
       -- proposito: aqui la hora la fija el desplegable. Puestos como papel
       -- temporal, la etiqueta no llegaba a la URL y las teselas salian 500 por
       -- pedirle al servidor un cubo de cuatro dimensiones.
       'init_time=' || $pasada || ',lead_time=' || $lead AS zarr_sel,
       CASE $capa
         WHEN 'total_cloud_cover_atmosphere'                THEN '0,100'
         WHEN 'temperature_2m'                              THEN '-10,35'
         WHEN 'relative_humidity_2m'                        THEN '0,100'
         WHEN 'precipitation_surface'                       THEN '0,0.0028'
         WHEN 'precipitable_water_atmosphere'               THEN '0,60'
         WHEN 'pressure_reduced_to_mean_sea_level'          THEN '98000,103000'
         WHEN 'downward_short_wave_radiation_flux_surface'  THEN '0,1000'
         WHEN 'wind_u_10m'                                  THEN '-15,15'
         ELSE '0,100'
       END AS zarr_rescale,
       -- Nubosidad y lluvia van con rampa de INTERVALOS en vez de nombre, porque
       -- son campos que son casi todo ceros y toda rampa con nombre es opaca de
       -- punta a punta: un cielo despejado pintaria una sabana solida sobre el
       -- mapa base y sobre las flechas. El alfa solo puede venir de la rampa, asi
       -- que la rampa viaja entera.
       --
       -- Los intervalos van en 0-255, NO en las unidades del almacen: el rango de
       -- arriba lleva el dato al byte primero, y la rampa colorea bytes.
       CASE $capa
         WHEN 'total_cloud_cover_atmosphere'                THEN nubes.rampa
         WHEN 'precipitation_surface'                       THEN lluvia.rampa
         WHEN 'temperature_2m'                              THEN 'turbo'
         WHEN 'relative_humidity_2m'                        THEN 'blues'
         WHEN 'precipitable_water_atmosphere'               THEN 'viridis'
         WHEN 'downward_short_wave_radiation_flux_surface'  THEN 'inferno'
         WHEN 'pressure_reduced_to_mean_sea_level'          THEN 'rdylbu'
         WHEN 'wind_u_10m'                                  THEN 'rdylbu'
         ELSE 'greys'
       END AS zarr_colormap
FROM nubes, lluvia
-- Cero filas cuando el desplegable dice `none`, y entonces el panel no arma
-- ningun dataset zarr y no hay raster que pintar.
WHERE $capa <> 'none'

panels.title: 10 m wind over ${capa:text} · ${hora} · newest GFS run

list.description: Where the repository lives. `stac+` rather than the bucket address: dynamical rolls the repository version and asks callers not to write it down, so the catalogue is asked where today's is.
list.label: Store
list.name: store

list.description: Which hour of the forecast the field shows. This is the only clock here: a flow field holds one instant, so the map's own time bar has nothing to walk.
list.label: Hour
list.name: hora
list.query:
-- The forecast hours, from now on, as a dropdown. `__text` is what is read and
-- `__value` what travels. The first option is the one Grafana takes by default,
-- so the WHERE trims the past and the dashboard opens on the current hour.
WITH run AS (SELECT to_timestamp(floor(epoch(now() - INTERVAL '9 hours') / 21600) * 21600) AS init)
SELECT strftime((init + INTERVAL '1 hour' * h) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC',
                '%d %b %H:%M UTC') AS __text,
       strftime((init + INTERVAL '1 hour' * h) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC',
                '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z') AS __value
FROM run, (SELECT unnest(range(0, 121)) AS h UNION ALL SELECT unnest(range(123, 385, 3)) AS h) g
WHERE init + INTERVAL '1 hour' * h >= date_trunc('hour', now())
ORDER BY h

list.description: Detail or reach, at the same price. Both are 49 points and both cost about seven seconds: what a request costs is the number of points, not the ground they cover.
list.label: Grid
list.name: paso

list.description: Which of the archive's own variables is painted under the wind. The archive has no wind speed — it publishes u and v components only — and the tile server paints one variable at a time, so this is a field beside the wind rather than the wind itself.
list.label: Under the wind
list.name: capa
list.query: Cloud cover (%) : total_cloud_cover_atmosphere,2 m temperature (C) : temperature_2m,2 m relative humidity (%) : relative_humidity_2m,Precipitation rate (kg m-2 s-1) : precipitation_surface,Precipitable water (kg m-2) : precipitable_water_atmosphere,Shortwave radiation (W m-2) : downward_short_wave_radiation_flux_surface,Pressure at MSL (Pa) : pressure_reduced_to_mean_sea_level,10 m wind U (m s-1) : wind_u_10m,Nothing : none

list.description: The run the field is read from.
list.label: Run
list.name: pasada
list.query:
-- The run the field is read from, with the usual nine-hour rule: GFS starts every
-- six hours and dynamical takes a while to ingest it, so the newest run that is
-- surely there is the last multiple of six hours that is already nine hours old.
SELECT strftime(to_timestamp(floor(epoch(now() - INTERVAL '9 hours') / 21600) * 21600)
                AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000000000')

list.description: The chosen hour as nanoseconds from the start of the run.
list.label: Lead
list.name: lead
list.query:
-- The chosen hour as a distance from the start of the run, in nanoseconds, which
-- is the unit `lead_time` answers to.
--
-- It comes straight from the dropdown, not from the map: the flow layer holds one
-- instant and has no clock of its own to publish.
--
-- OJO: in a VARIABLE query this datasource does NOT quote by itself -- it does in
-- panel queries -- so the quotes around '${hora}' are mine. And the arithmetic
-- rides on floor()'s DOUBLE: written over integers, 3600 * 1000000000 overflows
-- INT32 before anything else happens.
WITH run AS (
  SELECT to_timestamp(floor(epoch(now() - INTERVAL '9 hours') / 21600) * 21600) AS init
)
SELECT (least(greatest(floor(epoch(('${hora}')::TIMESTAMPTZ - init) / 3600), 0), 384)
        * 3600 * 1000000000)::BIGINT::VARCHAR
FROM run

title: NOAA GFS — wind field from an Icechunk repository
